definition.name: weak_schur_sampling
definition.definition: Weak Schur sampling is the quantum measurement obtained by measuring the Young diagram register Y after applying the Schur transform to rho^{tensor n}. The outcome is a Young diagram lambda with probability Pr[lambda] = dim(lambda) * s_lambda^d(rho), where s_lambda^d(rho) = tr(nu_lambda^d(rho)). Post-measurement, the state in the (P,Q) registers is rho|_lambda = |lambda><lambda| tensor (I_{dim(lambda)}/dim(lambda)) tensor (nu_lambda^d(rho)/s_lambda^d(rho)). Weak Schur sampling is 'non-destructive': E_lambda[rho|_lambda] = Schur^d rho^{tensor n} (Schur^d)^dag (Lemma 3.5).
